references.text: The original Passover ordinance given to Moses and the children of Israel in Egypt, which is the basis for the Passover command repeated in Numbers 9:4.
Moses instructs the elders of Israel to slaughter the Passover lamb, parallel to his instruction to all Israel to keep the Passover.
The children of Israel did as the Lord had commanded Moses and Aaron, a parallel formula of obedience to their response to the Passover command.
The Passover regulation in the holiness code that sets the time for celebrating Passover on the fourteenth day of the first month.
Moses repeats the Passover command to the children of Israel in Deuteronomy, confirming the enduring obligation to keep the Passover.
The children of Israel kept the Passover at Gilgal after entering the promised land, fulfilling Moses' instructions.
King Hezekiah sent a message to all Israel to come and keep the Passover, in line with the tradition from Moses.
King Josiah kept the Passover and instructed the Levites to prepare themselves, based on Moses' original command.
Those who had returned from captivity kept the Passover and continued the tradition that Moses had established.
